question: Does satisfying a traffic signal warrant automatically require installation of a traffic control signal?
model_answer: Direct Answer: No. The MUTCD explicitly states that satisfying one or more signal warrants does not by itself require installing a traffic control signal. Warrant satisfaction is only one factor in an engineering study, and agencies should consider alternatives to signalization even where warrants are met. Standards (mandatory): - "The satisfaction of a traffic signal warrant or warrants shall not in itself require the installation of a traffic control signal." - Analogously for stop control: "The satisfaction of an all-way stop control warrant or warrants shall not in itself require the installation of all-way stop control at an unsignalized intersection." Guidance (recommended): - "Since road user delay and the frequency of some types of crashes are sometimes higher under traffic signal control than under STOP sign control, consideration should be given to providing alternatives to traffic control signals even if one or more of the signal warrants (see Chapter 4C) has been satisfied." - Where a signal is installed based on projected (estimated) traffic volumes, except when Warrant 8 is the basis, an engineering study should be done within 1 year of putting the signal into steady (stop-and-go) operation to determine if the signal is justified; if not justified, the signal should be taken out of steady operation or removed. Support (informational): - The safe and efficient movement of all road users is the primary consideration in the engineering study; satisfaction of a warrant is one relevant factor "but it is not intended to be the only factor or even the overriding consideration." Agencies can also install a signal where no warrants are met, but only after an engineering study documents the rationale that a signal is the best solution. - The Crash Experience warrant illustrates that warrants define conditions for *considering* a signal (where crash severity and frequency are the principal reasons to consider installation), not for mandating one. Visual evidence: [Image 8] shows Section 4B.03, Alternatives to Traffic Control Signals, which lists alternative treatments (e.g., warning signs, roundabouts, pedestrian hybrid beacons, speed reduction measures, flashing beacons) that should be considered even when signal warrants are satisfied. Citations: - Section 4C.01 Standard §3 (p.651) - Section 2B.12 Standard §5 (p.79) - Section 4B.03 Guidance §1 (p.649) - Section 4C.01 Guidance §12 (p.652) - Section 4C.01 Support §20 (p.653) - Section 4C.08 Support §1 (p.661) - Page 690
gold_answer: No. A warrant is a threshold that triggers analysis; it is not conclusive justification. Installation must be based on an engineering study considering safety, operation, alternatives, and the site. A signal can also be installed where no warrant is met if an engineering study documents why it is the best solution.
